subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the space complexity of an algorithm measure?
options: The size of the output file only
The amount of memory it uses relative to input size
questions.explain: Space complexity describes memory growth as a function of input size.

questions.q: In functional programming, the higher-order function 'map' does what?
options: Reduces a list to a single accumulated value
Sorts a list into ascending order
Applies a given function to every element of a list, returning a new list
Selects only elements that satisfy a predicate
questions.explain: map applies a function to each element of a list and returns a new list of the transformed results.

questions.q: Which paradigm expresses logic as facts and rules, with the system inferring answers to queries (e.g. Prolog)?
questions.explain: Logic (declarative) programming states facts and rules and lets an inference engine derive results from queries.

questions.q: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search on n items?
questions.explain: In the worst case linear search examines every one of the n items.

questions.q: Bubble sort is best described as comparing and swapping which elements?
options: The first and last elements only
Elements separated by a fixed gap
questions.explain: Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order pairs until sorted.

questions.q: The 'reduce' (fold) higher-order function is used to:
options: Combine the elements of a list into a single accumulated value
Return a new list of the same length
Reverse the order of a list
questions.explain: reduce repeatedly applies a combining function to accumulate the list's elements into one result value.

questions.q: Which traversal would you use to explore as far as possible before backtracking?
questions.explain: DFS goes deep along each branch, backtracking when it can go no further.

questions.q: Which development methodology emphasises iterative delivery, frequent customer feedback and adapting to changing requirements?
questions.explain: Agile delivers software in short iterations, embracing changing requirements and continuous customer collaboration.

questions.q: Which sorting algorithm has a worst-case time complexity of O(n^2) but is efficient on nearly-sorted data?
questions.explain: Insertion sort runs close to O(n) when the list is almost sorted.

questions.q: Quicksort has which worst-case time complexity, typically when pivots are poorly chosen?
questions.explain: With consistently bad pivots quicksort degrades to quadratic time.

questions.q: In object-oriented programming, what does encapsulation primarily achieve?
options: Creating multiple instances from one class definition
Allowing one method name to behave differently for different object types
Bundling data and the methods that act on it, hiding internal state behind an interface
Allowing a subclass to acquire attributes and methods of a superclass
questions.explain: Encapsulation binds attributes and methods together within a class and restricts direct external access to the internal data.

questions.q: Which precondition must hold for binary search to work correctly?
options: The data must contain no duplicates
The data must be stored in a linked list
questions.explain: Binary search relies on order to discard half the data at each comparison.

questions.q: Which statement about passing a parameter by value is correct?
options: A copy of the data is made, so changes inside the subroutine do not affect the original
The subroutine can permanently alter the caller's original variable
Only arrays may be passed this way
The variable's address is shared with the subroutine
questions.explain: By value passes a copy, so modifications within the subroutine leave the caller's original variable unchanged.

questions.q: In the software development life cycle, which model proceeds through fixed sequential stages with little overlap or return to earlier phases?
questions.explain: The waterfall model moves linearly through distinct phases, each completed before the next begins.

questions.q: A class can be described as:
options: A specific instance occupying memory at run time
A template or blueprint defining the attributes and methods of objects
questions.explain: A class is a template specifying the attributes and methods that its objects (instances) will have.

questions.q: Alpha testing differs from beta testing in that alpha testing is:
options: Performed by a wide public audience after release
Carried out in-house by the development team or testers before release to users
questions.explain: Alpha testing is conducted internally before release, whereas beta testing is done by selected external users.

questions.q: What is the worst-case time complexity of binary search on a sorted array of n elements?
questions.explain: Binary search halves the search space each step, giving logarithmic time.

questions.q: In functional programming, 'immutability' means that:
options: Once created, data values cannot be changed
Functions cannot be passed as arguments
questions.explain: Immutability means data cannot be altered after creation; transformations produce new values instead.

questions.q: Which graph traversal uses a queue to visit nodes level by level?
questions.explain: Breadth-first search uses a queue to explore neighbours before going deeper.

questions.q: What is the best-case time complexity of bubble sort with an early-exit optimisation on an already-sorted list?
questions.explain: With a swap flag, one clean pass over n elements detects a sorted list in O(n).

questions.q: What does polymorphism mean in object-oriented programming?
options: Hiding implementation detail from the user
The ability for the same method call to take many forms depending on the object's type
Restricting access to an object's internal data
Defining a class as a template for objects
questions.explain: Polymorphism literally means 'many forms', allowing a single interface or method name to behave differently across object types.

questions.q: Selection in programming is implemented by which type of construct?
questions.explain: Selection chooses between paths of execution using conditional constructs such as IF or CASE.

questions.q: How does the A* algorithm improve on Dijkstra's algorithm?
options: It only works on unweighted graphs
It uses a heuristic to guide the search toward the goal
questions.explain: A* adds an admissible heuristic estimate to direct the search efficiently.

questions.q: Removing unnecessary detail to focus on the essential elements of a problem is known as what?
questions.explain: Abstraction hides irrelevant detail to manage complexity.

questions.q: A problem solvable in polynomial time is best described as which of the following?
questions.explain: Tractable problems have polynomial-time solutions considered feasible.

questions.q: Big-O notation describes which characteristic of an algorithm?
options: The amount of disk space on the computer
Its asymptotic growth rate as input size increases
The number of lines of code
questions.explain: Big-O expresses how resource use scales with input size, ignoring constants.

questions.q: What is an intractable problem?
options: One that cannot be expressed as an algorithm
One that only computers in the cloud can solve
One that always runs in constant time
One with no known polynomial-time algorithm
questions.explain: Intractable problems lack any practical polynomial-time solution as n grows.

questions.q: Which complexity class grows fastest as n increases?
questions.explain: Exponential growth O(2^n) outpaces logarithmic, linear and quadratic growth.

questions.q: A breadth-first traversal of a tree visits nodes in what order?
options: All nodes at one depth before moving to the next depth
questions.explain: BFS processes a tree level by level using a queue.

questions.q: Which programming paradigm is characterised by writing programs as a sequence of statements that change program state, using procedures/subroutines?
questions.explain: Procedural programming structures code as ordered statements grouped into procedures that operate on shared mutable state.
